summary: sc-wizard resolves its sole dependency from an off-registry tarball URL
details: package.json declares the package's only dependency `ltidisafe` as a direct HTTPS tarball URL (`https://ltidi.storage.googleapis.com/depenconf/ltidisafe-4.0.1.tgz`) rather than a registry version range. On `npm install`, npm fetches that URL and installs whatever bytes it returns, executing any lifecycle scripts contained in the fetched tarball — unpinned, integrity-unchecked, and outside the npm registry's publish controls. The shipped `index.js` is an empty stub, so the manifest-declared off-registry URL is effectively the entire install-time payload. The dependency source is a mutable third-party storage bucket; whoever controls that URL controls code running on the installer's machine at install time. The high version number (`99.9.1`) relative to a short, generic name is consistent with a dependency-confusion lure intended to win resolution against an internal `sc-wizard` package.
